“Pulaski Policy Papers” is a series of publications that focus on issues of great importance to Poland’s safety and stability, such as: global economy, Poland’s foreign policy and the political situation in Central and Eastern Europe.

The editor-in-chief of the Pulaski Policy Papers is Mr. Tomasz Smura (tsmura@pulaski.pl).

Published: August 26, 2026

What do Poland and the Republic of Korea (ROK) have in common? Despite the distance between the two and the fact that they are representative of and stand as the most successful nations economically, politically and militarily in their respective regions of the world, despite the two nations being the products of two entirely different cultures, the answer to that question of what they have in common is “a great deal.”

item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-25

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.

Abbas spoke of a genocidal war in Gaza, warned that the very existence of the Palestinian people is now under threat, and appealed to Donald Trump to honour his commitment to prevent the annexation of Palestinian land.

Rwandan Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva said that the Organization is better at responding to crises than at preventing them, and that institutions earn legitimacy through results rather than promises.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres spoke of four challenges linked to the exercise of power, namely war, inequality, climate change and artificial intelligence.

item.content:encoded:
The Ukrainians are overwhelming Moscow’s air defence. Day 1672 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-25

Russian forces continued their offensive on most fronts in Donetsk Oblast, but failed to make significant progress.Between Dobropillia and Druzhkivka, and between Kostiantynivka and Chasiv Yar, however, there was a noticeable widening of the grey zone, which should be linked to the gradual withdrawal of Ukrainian forces from areas where the military significance of holding their positions had been lost and where they risked being cut off from their main forces. The reinforcement of Ukrainian forces in the Dobropillia area with sub-units of the 425th Separate Assault Regiment “Skelya” and the 225th Assault Regiment allowed for a brief stabilisation of the situation and the recapture of some positions. After 20 September, the Russians resumed their offensive there, entering the town from the south, whilst their sabotage and reconnaissance groups appeared in the areas to the west and north of it. The situation north of Lyman has relatively stabilised, although according to some sources, Ukrainian forces have attempted to cross to the eastern bank of the Zherebets River.

Russian advances have forced the expansion of the mandatory evacuation zone for families with children in Donetsk Oblast.It covers parts of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, as well as nine other towns. The evacuation order covers 41.5% of the area of the former and 10% of the latter. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Latvian parliamentary election: Prime Minister seeks re-election

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-25

The United List (Latvian:Apvienotais saraksts, AS), led by incumbent Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, is likely to win the 3 October election to the Saeima, Latvia’s 100-seat unicameral parliament. His appointment in May this year, which brought a series of coalition crises to an end, shifted voter preferences and prompted a suddensurge in support for AS in the polls. Previously, when Evika Siliņa of New Unity (Jaunā Vienotība, JV) headed the government, opinion polls had indicated growing support for Latvia First (Latvian:Latvija pirmajā vietā, LPV), a populist party led by oligarch Ainārs Šlesers, which has centred its campaign on criticism of JV.

The shift in voter preferences this summer largely reflects Prime Minister Kulbergs’s effective management of his public image and political messaging. He has not only successfully distanced himself from his predecessors’ mistakes but has also appropriated the populist opposition’s key message: the promise of effective government. Socio-economic issues have dominated this year’s election campaign, while regional security has remained a secondary concern.
